layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: the at-large congressional district, the whole state

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; one feature, measured 2026-11-12: Delaware elects one representative from the whole state, so the one district is the state, which TIGER names "Congressional District (at Large)" (CD120 "00") and the card prints by that name. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same district, so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 3 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 3 features, measured 2026-11-12. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Delaware's three counties are governed three ways: New Castle by an elected county executive and county council, Kent by an elected levy court and Sussex by an elected county council, and each also elects officers such as a sheriff, a recorder of deeds and a register of wills. No list of them was read in this pass, so the card says which form the county has and names nobody. Recorded as gap de-county-officials.

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 16 features for Delaware, measured 2026-11-12: 16 school districts. TIGERweb's secondary and elementary layers carry nothing for Delaware, so they are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap de-school-board-members.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 21 features, measured 2026-11-12, identical to the 2024 vintage (layer 5) that day. The chambers do not nest, so each map is simplified on its own. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: de-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the General Assembly's own member tables (legis.delaware.gov, the data its Senate member page draws its table from, asked the way the page asks): each senator's name, party and page on the General Assembly's own site. The tables carry no e-mail address or telephone, and their own member links go to the party caucuses' sites, which are partisan and are never linked.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 70 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Delaware (236 in the app's bounding box), about 72 km2 of land on average, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Delaware (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='10'. The app's box reaches into Maryland, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, and measured 2026-11-12, 70 of the 236 ZCTAs in it reach into Delaware and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Delaware. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City, Town or Village
layers.rank_note: 57 incorporated cities, towns and villages, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city, town or village containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 57 records: 44 towns, 10 cities and 3 villages, every one an active government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF DELAWARE IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY, TOWN OR VILLAGE (about 8% of its land, 393.1 of 5,046.8 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Delaware's local officials was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap de-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 109 points in Delaware's envelope, which reaches into Maryland, Pennsylvania and New Jersey; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Delaware — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Legislative Hall, 411 Legislative Avenue, Dover, Kent County

negative_point.note: the Atlantic Ocean east of Rehoboth Beach — outside Delaware and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names no state here, because it is open water (control: the Legislative Hall returns Delaware), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does, nor any outline in the change that opens the last thirteen states. IT IS OPEN WATER, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Delaware outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (3 counties).
Delaware's 3 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The one U.S. House district, the whole state ("Congressional District (at Large)"), TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same as layer 4 (CD119).
The 21 Delaware Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper).
The 41 Delaware House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Delaware elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from de/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
